reviewMethod: Parent canonical selection of pinned provisional assistant reviews. Five audit disagreements quarantined; seven audited positives use proposed audit intervals only. Forty legacy normals are replaced by explicit every-frame-reviewed 0-4 second spans. Seventeen prior dense normals and round3 accepted reviews are retained without extrapolation.
limitations: All labels remain provisional assistant still-image judgments, not human ground truth or full-motion review.
Unaudited old positive intervals retain sampled-review uncertainty. Audited events do not validate original boundaries outside inspected spans.
Unknown tails remain unknown. Positive window eligibility requires at least half annotated coverage; contextual frames outside events are not normal labels.
All VID is one unresolved actor/session training cohort. No calibration, holdout, night/IR or 50-100-person accuracy evidence is supplied.
Original source reviews preserve detailed methods, rights, notes and limitations; their hashes and selected JSON pointers are recorded here.

recordings.notes: Retained central subset shows close upper-body gripping, turning and paired torso displacement; corroborated by 32 sequentially decoded source-frame samples. Portions around 2.9-3.6s are partly occluded by the nearer body, so precise grip and uninterrupted continuity remain uncertain. Omit initial arm swings and late bend/release; no impact/force inference.

Retained central samples show a low/kneeling person with two standing people holding/reaching into the upper-body/arm region; the low body is displaced and remains bent while close contact recurs across the interval. Omit initial drop and later repositioning. No props apparent in inspected samples; exact continuity, force and event boundaries remain provisional.

Retained central subset repeatedly shows two foreground people making upper-body/forearm contact, leaning and pushing/turning together, then one bends low. Other people interact behind them. Omit the opening approach and later separated arm movements/repositioning. No props apparent in inspected samples; continuity and precise boundaries are provisional and no impact/force inference is made.

Repeated adjacent samples show one person bent with hands near the face while the other reaches to and contacts the head/shoulder region and forearms. Retain the central paired contact configurations; omit both edge margins. Actual impacts and continuity between samples are unverified. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

The enlarged source-image crop resolves repeated upper-arm/shoulder and clothing grips, with braced legs, leaning torsos and visible pulling configurations. Retain the central contact span, omitting initial approach and the final margin. Clothing fabric is visible; no separate handheld prop is resolved in the inspected samples. Exact force, impacts and continuous motion are not established. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

The enlarged crop shows repeated head/shoulder contact and upper-body holds as the pair turn and lean together in the late central span. Earlier arm extensions, gaps and approach are omitted. The samples support contact configurations, not verified impacts or continuous motion. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

Across adjacent samples, the foreground pair maintain repeated forearm, chest/shoulder and head contact while bracing and changing body angle; another person is initially bent nearby. Retain the central paired contact sequence and omit the final turning/occluded margin. No specific injury or intent is inferred. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

One central person is held at the upper body, bends down and is later on the floor while nearby people repeatedly lean over and contact the upper body/limbs. Retain this central-to-late contact span; exclude the initial approach and last margin. Transition to the floor and any individual impact are only sampled, not continuously verified. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

Adjacent samples show repeated head/upper-shoulder grips with the paired bodies leaning and turning together. Retain the early central contact episode; later arm extensions and greater separation are unannotated. Apparent strikes are not confirmed as impacts. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

The late central samples show a head/upper-body hold and continued arm contact while one person repeatedly bends and steps around the other. Retain that visible subset. Earlier contact is separated by a rear-view occlusion/turning segment, so it is not joined to this interval. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

Enlarged source crops show a central person bent forward with a nearby person holding the upper shoulder/head region across adjacent samples; a third person repeatedly reaches toward that region. Retain the sustained central holding configurations, omitting beginning and separation margins. Raised hands do not independently prove an impact. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

A standing person wraps an arm around the seated person's head/upper shoulders, with continued paired bending and subsequent rise from the chair in adjacent samples. Retain only the visible holding/rising span; omit approach and later separation. The exact transition and applied force remain unverified. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

Across the retained central frames a standing person maintains an upper-body grip on a seated/crouched person while their torsos repeatedly bend and move together. Other people are present. The interval is a provisional subset of the longer interaction; omit the initial approach and final hand-obstructed margin.

A person behind the seated person maintains an upper-body/head hold as the seated torso twists and lowers toward the floor; contact continues in the sampled lower positions. Retain the central sustained restraint/grappling configurations. Bystanders hold small devices; no interaction weapon is resolved in the retained samples. Omit clip edges and avoid impact claims. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

The central pair repeatedly wrap arms around each other's torso/head, bend and rotate together, then lower toward the floor. Clear paired grips recur across adjacent samples through the retained span. Omit beginning and last margin; motion continuity and individual impacts are not verified. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

A standing person holds the seated person around the head/upper torso throughout adjacent sampled views, while another person reaches and contacts the shoulder/arms. Retain the central sustained contact span; omit clip edges. Do not infer the purpose of the additional person's actions or actual strike impacts. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

The early central pair show a head/upper-shoulder hold from behind, repeated bent postures and chair/body displacement across adjacent samples. Retain this relatively unobstructed contact span. Later arriving people obscure the interaction, so the crowd sequence is unannotated. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

The pair remain connected at the head/upper torso as one person repeatedly bends low and the other braces with extended arms. Retain the early central holding configurations; later arm exchanges and increasing separation are omitted. Impacts and force are not established from the samples. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

One person maintains a visible upper-back/head grip while the other bends progressively and then crouches/puts hands on the floor. Adjacent frames repeatedly show the paired grip and constrained body positions. Retain the central span, excluding initial arm gestures and final edge; the lowering motion is not continuously reviewed. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.

Two central people repeatedly hold/contact each other's upper arms and shoulders while turning and bracing, visible across adjacent sampled frames. Retain the central paired contact configurations; omit the early approach and final edge of the clip. No specific strike, intent or injury is established.

Central adjacent views show a compact group with repeated forearm/shoulder grips, braced stances and people bending/turning together. Retain the clearest central physical-contact sequence; omit later separation and less clear margins. Occlusion limits which pair is in contact at each instant; no individual strike or intent is established. Provisional assistant sampled-frame screening; motion was not continuously viewed.
One person holds another across upper torso from behind while a third repeatedly reaches/contact the front; leaning and bracing persist through central samples.
Central pair remain joined across upper torso/shoulders while another person repeatedly contacts their arms and torso; omit late release and leg extension.
Three standing people repeatedly reach/contact the shoulders and upper body of a crouched person; central samples show close joined bodies and repeated downward arm positions. Omit later separation.
Repeated upper-body/shoulder grips and bent, jointly rotating torsos in central samples. Omit setup and late uncertain margin.
Three people remain in repeated upper-arm/shoulder grips with bent torsos and shared turns through central samples; retain central interaction and omit later reconfiguration.
Pair repeatedly grip forearms/shoulders while one bends at the waist, then re-engage in an upright-to-bent contact sequence. Separate the two retained spans around an uncertain transition.
Two people on the floor remain joined through upper bodies/arms, shifting between crouched and side-lying configurations. Retain central ground-contact imagery; omit setup and final loosening.

Three-person contact develops into a crouched group near desks; repeated shoulder/upper-body grips, joined bending and lowering configurations support the central interval. Omit early approach and late lift/release margin.
Two foreground people repeatedly grip upper arms/shoulders with bent torsos and shared rotation; later a third joins. Retain central paired span and leave later boundary unannotated.
Foreground pair repeatedly grip around shoulders/upper arms while torsos bend and rotate together; retain central joined span and omit late separation.

Two central people remain closely joined at shoulders/upper arms through the retained samples, with repeated bent torsos, pulling-like arm configurations and shared rotation. Retain only the sustained close-contact portion; surrounding observers do not supply additional positive events.

Repeated sampled views show a standing person leaning over and gripping the upper body of a seated person, with substantial sideways chair/body displacement. Retain the central contact span; omit the early setup and late release. Continuity and force are not independently measured.
Central samples show repeated arm/shoulder contact, bracing and bent torsos among the pair and nearby third person. Retain central contact sequence, omit final separation.

One person moves beside an orange door, closes it and lowers into a seat by shelves. Provisional normal selection applies only to the densely observed 0-4 s interval; unknown tail remains unannotated.
